chapter: Early New Orleans music and Mardi Gras
title: Buddy Bolden as a strong trumpet player
summary: Williams heard Buddy Bolden around 1905-06 and describes him as a strong trumpet player who played at halls; he visited the city since 1902.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I see. Let me think of some of the other old trumpet players. Who else did you hear, say around 1905? Do you remember any other trumpet players?
Not 1905, no. I hadn't started playing no music myself.
Well one time you mentioned Buddy Bolin to me. I just…

Buddy Bolin, I was quite young when he played. That might be around 1905 or 1906. But I heard him play it several times. He was a strong trumpet player. He was a strong trumpet player. He had that Jackson Street Hall, Long Termin Hall, and he hadn't played well at that Lincoln Park. You know he could blow.
Oh yeah. Well did you hear him here in the city or out in the country? Yeah. Oh you used to come in sometimes, huh?
